scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The study presents a clear, well-scoped evaluation paradigm designed to mitigate data contamination in generative scientific discovery benchmarks. Its negative and nuanced empirical results are thoroughly grounded by objective baselines, statistical significance tests, and detailed qualitative error analyses.

decklists. Across both domains, models produce
plausible outputs, but few align with real-world

matched 10 of 40 real innovations with 166 ideas
proposed across runs. In MTG, the best deck from
Gemini 3 Flash recovered 5 of 7 new-set cards
from the third-place PT deck, and across all 108
decks, the cards models selected most often were

suggest that a key capability gap for AI scientists
is not idea generation, but filtering, prioritization,
and coherent novelty.

Contributions.
• We propose a framework for evaluating AI scientists'
capabilities with adversarial fast-moving real-world
domains.
• We instantiate a proof of concept of the framework
in two structurally distinct domains, Formula 1 car
design under new technical regulations and Magic: The
Gathering deck construction under evolving cards.
• We identify failure modes that are informative for
AI scientist evaluation, including the production of
plausible-but-misaligned ideas, and systematic blind
spots for value that arises from complex surrounding
contexts.

Our framework evaluates AI scientist capabilities through a
time-delayed generation task. For each domain, we define
an information cutoff t and construct a fixed input corpus
containing only material available before that point, such
as rules, constraints, public context, and relevant prior ex-
amples. The AI system is then asked to generate structured
candidate artifacts from this corpus, such as ideas, designs,
or solutions. These generations are evaluated against post-
cutoff artifacts produced by real-world experts. This cre-
ates a prospective-style evaluation of whether models can
generate non-trivial ideas under realistic constraints, while
removing the risk of information leakage.

evidence.excerpt:
F1 is the pinnacle of motorsport and is fiercely innovative.
Most often, the fastest car wins, and hence there is signif-
icant engineering investment from teams to develop new
ideas that shave tenths of a second off lap times. In 2026,
the FIA Formula 1 Technical Regulations went through the
largest change in history. Teams have had to design new
cars from the ground up to comply with these regulations.
The corpus contained a 264-page PDF document FIA 2026
Section CTechnical Regulations, dated 10th of December
2025. The task was to produce technical innovations spe-
cific to the 2026 cars. Ground truth was a curated set of 40
real F1 concepts drawn from publicly available pre-season
analysis (Appendix Table 2).

evidence.excerpt:
Novelty matching in the F1 domain utilized three stages.
First, generated ideas and real innovations were embedded
and shortlisted using a dual top-k retrieval strategy (k= 3),
retaining the nearest real innovations for each generated
idea and the nearest generated ideas for each real innovation.
Shortlisted pairs were assessed by an LLM judge (GPT-5.5)
for MATCH, PARTIAL, or NO MATCH. Candidate matches
then underwent human review to verify if the idea described
a similar physical effect to the real innovation. In parallel,
each generated idea was assessed along three quality dimen-
sions: citation accuracy, rule compliance, and engineering
plausibility. An idea was treated as passing these quality fil-
ters only if its cited regulations were substantively accurate,
its design was legal or plausibly within a regulatory grey
zone, and its mechanism was physically plausible.
MTG

domains can provide a practical intermediate test bed for
evaluating AI scientist capabilities. Across both domains,

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: MTG results rest on deterministic card overlap with tournament-tested expert decklists, while F1 matches are confirmed by a human reviewer blinded to the LLM judge's discrete verdict [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0024, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by deterministic decklist comparisons against official Pro Tour decks in MTG and by human adjudication of generated F1 ideas against real 2026 pre-season engineering innovations [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0024, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The systems under study are six frontier LLMs run through fixed three-agent prompt pipelines with no parameter fine-tuning, reward optimization, or iterative selection against the test tasks [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0020, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0021].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings closely reflect the evidence: models generate plausible ideas but struggle with filtering and complex contextual dependencies [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0003, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0039]. The authors explicitly document that 89% of LLM-judge shortlisted F1 pairs were downgraded upon human review and that aggregate MTG deck discovery only modestly exceeded random baselines [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0039, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0065].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Outputs are evaluated against real-world post-cutoff expert artifacts: 40 actual 2026 F1 innovations and 19 Magic: The Gathering Pro Tour tournament decklists [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0017, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0019]. The evaluation incorporates calibrated hypergeometric random baselines, blinded human adjudication over candidate matches, and thorough statistical testing (Fisher's exact, Wilcoxon, Friedman, Spearman correlation) [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0024, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0027, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: MTG evaluations rely on deterministic card-matching against official tournament decklists, and F1 comparisons are corroborated by independent human review of technical mechanisms against real pre-season engineering solutions [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0024, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic decklist comparisons against tournament-tested Pro Tour decks in MTG, and blinded human adjudication against real-world 2026 F1 pre-season engineering innovations [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0023, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0024, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Prompt-based three-agent decomposition pipelines run without parameter fine-tuning or iterative reward optimization on the test tasks [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0020, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0021].

primary.limitations: The authors candidly acknowledge that matching real innovations does not prove internal reasoning parity, expert outputs form an incomplete ground truth, proxy domains differ from pure scientific research, and human review was conducted by a non-expert single author [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0043, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology utilizes fixed-corpus prompting of six frontier LLMs whose training cutoffs predate the public disclosure of the reference artifacts, structured through a three-agent decomposition pipeline [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0020, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0057]. The prompt designs, pipeline configurations (general vs component-focused; one-shot vs tool-use), and retrieval shortlisting protocols are clearly defined and accompanied by code/data repositories [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0021, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0023].
primary.quality_rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped evaluation paradigm designed to mitigate data contamination in generative scientific discovery benchmarks. Its negative and nuanced empirical results are thoroughly grounded by objective baselines, statistical significance tests, and detailed qualitative error analyses.
primary.scoped_contribution: Bolton and Torr propose an evaluation framework for AI scientist capabilities using fast-moving, adversarial real-world domains with time-delayed reveal events, instantiated on Formula 1 2026 regulations and Magic: The Gathering deck construction [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0005, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0012].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped evaluation paradigm designed to mitigate data contamination in generative scientific discovery benchmarks. Its negative and nuanced empirical results are thoroughly grounded by objective baselines, statistical significance tests, and detailed qualitative error analyses.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors candidly acknowledge that matching real innovations does not prove internal reasoning parity, expert outputs form an incomplete ground truth, proxy domains differ from pure scientific research, and human review was conducted by a non-expert single author [E67304abafdac3dc0-B0043, E67304abafdac3dc0-B0063].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
